note: Reference pack: garden history styles, designers and garden buildings (site-neutral). Existing site ids (capability-brown, john-cheere, william-chambers, batty-langley, william-iii, crystal-palace, chatsworth-great-conservatory, kew-pagoda, chinese-designs-book) are defined by the site and not repeated here. Dates verified against web sources in October 2026; see Sources lines in the notes.

things.name: the gardens of Versailles
things.who: designed by André Le Nôtre for Louis XIV

things.name: the French formal garden style
things.who: developed in France by Le Nôtre and others

things.name: Het Loo palace gardens
things.who: palace built 1684–1686 for William of Orange; the garden followed from about 1686

things.name: the Hampton Court Great Fountain Garden (William and Mary)
things.who: remodelled for William and Mary, with Daniel Marot as designer

things.name: the Dutch formal garden style in England
things.who: brought to England after 1688 with William III

things.name: the formal woodland garden (wildernesses and rides)
things.who: a style of early eighteenth century English gardens

things.name: the gardens at Stowe
things.who: worked on by Bridgeman (from 1711), Kent (from 1730) and Brown (1741–1751), among others

things.name: the English landscape garden style
things.who: developed by Bridgeman, Kent and others from the 1720s

things.name: the ha-ha
things.who: a sunken wall and ditch that keeps livestock out without blocking the view; Stowe has what the National Trust calls England's first

things.name: the Serpentine in Hyde Park
things.who: made for Queen Caroline

things.name: the Picturesque movement
things.who: promoted by Price and Knight against Brown's smooth style

things.name: Repton's Red Books
things.who: bound client reports with before-and-after watercolours

things.name: the Victorian formal garden revival
things.who: revived by Barry, Nesfield and others

things.name: Victorian bedding schemes
things.who: massed tender plants raised in greenhouses and set out for summer

things.name: orangery and greenhouse heating methods
things.who: hot-water heating, first used in a British hothouse by Count Chabannes in 1816, developed by Bacon and Atkinson from 1822, and Perkins in 1831

things.name: the glass excise duty
things.who: an excise duty on glass by weight, which made large panes dear

things.name: the repeal of the glass tax
things.who: the abolition of the excise duty on glass

things.name: garden buildings and follies
things.who: temples, pavilions and eye-catchers in designed landscapes

things.name: garden cold plunge baths
things.who: small buildings with a cold-water pool, thought good for health

things.name: garden hermitages
things.who: rustic cells and ruins for contemplation

things.name: chinoiserie in English gardens
things.who: European taste for Chinese-style buildings and ornament

things.name: the Willow Pattern
things.who: developed by English potters (Caughley about 1780, Spode about 1790; sources disagree)

things.name: lead garden statuary
things.who: cast in London yards and often painted to look like stone

things.name: trompe-l'œil painting
things.who: painting that tricks the eye into seeing real objects or depth

things.name: orangeries in general
things.who: frost-free buildings for citrus trees in tubs

people.name: André Le Nôtre
people.who: Louis XIV's royal gardener and the designer of Vaux-le-Vicomte and Versailles
events: began the gardens of Vaux-le-Vicomte
was summoned to Versailles by Louis XIV

people.name: Charles Bridgeman
people.who: a garden designer who linked formal and landscape styles and became royal gardener
events: began work at Stowe
became royal gardener
made the Serpentine in Hyde Park

people.name: William Kent
people.who: a painter, architect and garden designer, creator of Rousham and the Elysian Fields at Stowe
events: began work at Stowe
began to develop the gardens at Rousham

people.name: Humphry Repton
people.who: the landscape gardener who succeeded Brown and made the Red Books
events: set up as a landscape gardener
published Sketches and Hints on Landscape Gardening

people.name: Sir Joseph Paxton
people.who: the head gardener at Chatsworth who designed the Great Conservatory and the Crystal Palace (Britannica gives his birth as 1801)
events: became head gardener at Chatsworth
first flowered the giant Amazon water lily in Britain
designed the Crystal Palace

people.name: William Andrews Nesfield
people.who: the leading designer of Victorian parterres de broderie
events: retired from the army and turned to watercolours
laid out gardens at Castle Howard

people.name: Sir Charles Barry
people.who: architect of the Houses of Parliament and designer of Italianate terraced gardens
events: began the Italianate gardens at Trentham
began the gardens at Shrubland Park

people.name: Andrew Carpenter
people.who: a French-born lead statue maker who had worked for Nost and set up near Hyde Park Corner
events: was working independently near Hyde Park Corner
announced he would stop casting lead figures

people.name: John (Jan) Nost the elder
people.who: a Flemish sculptor from Mechelen who ran the leading London lead statue yard
events: began to specialise in lead garden figures

people.name: John Nost II (Van Nost the younger)
people.who: the sculptor who ran the Nost lead statue yard after 1710
events: took over the Nost yard
